relation_statement: The offloaded gradient accumulation buffer must conserve the sum of per-microbatch gradients across all microsteps of one global step when gradient_accumulation_steps > 1 under ZeRO-2 with CPU offload.
observable_signal: accumulated gradient norm/checksum at the accumulation boundary vs the running sum of per-microstep gradients
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 2 with CPU-offload optimizer and gradient_accumulation_steps > 1
evidence_from_issue: ZeRO-2 + CPU offload micro_step_id off-by-one and wrong copy/accumulate gating
evidence_from_fix: copy/accumulate gating used `not is_gradient_accumulation_boundary` for copy, which copies on every non-boundary microstep instead of only the first

relation_statement: The z-loss under reduction='mean' must equal the scalar masked mean of z_squared over non-ignored tokens whenever labels contain ignore_index tokens.
observable_signal: z-loss value (and shape: scalar vs vector) compared against a reference masked-mean recomputed from the same logits and labels
validity_precondition: compute_z_loss=True with reduction='mean' and labels containing ignore_index (-100) tokens
evidence_from_issue: cross_entropy_loss z-loss reduction='mean' uses wrong masked-mean formula
evidence_from_fix: buggy: z_squared / (labels != ignore).mean() returns vector divided by scalar, wrong scaling; fix: (z_squared * (labels != ignore)).mean() returns scalar masked-mean

relation_statement: The auxiliary z-loss must be normalized by batch_size_in_tokens rather than num_micro_batches whenever softmax_auxiliary_loss is enabled.
observable_signal: ratio of z-loss to main loss, which inflates by batch_size_in_tokens/num_micro_batches under the buggy normalizer
validity_precondition: softmax_auxiliary_loss=True and num_micro_batches != batch_size_in_tokens
evidence_from_issue: Trainer.train_micro_batch divides z_loss by num_micro_batches instead of batch_size_in_tokens
evidence_from_fix: z_loss / num_micro_batches scales auxiliary loss by gradient accumulation count, not by token count; with T >> num_micro_batches, z_loss dominates loss and corrupts training

relation_statement: The input gradient of a tensor-parallel linear layer with frozen weight must be all-reduced so it is identical across all TP ranks after backward.
observable_signal: cross-rank checksum of grad_input within the TP group after the frozen-weight linear backward
validity_precondition: linear layers whose weight has requires_grad=False (frozen), linear_with_frozen_weight code path
evidence_from_issue: LinearWithFrozenWeight backward forgets to all-reduce grad_input across TP
evidence_from_fix: backward returns grad_input without all-reducing across TP ranks; each rank only sees its column-shard of grad

relation_statement: Every rank in a model-parallel group must receive the training batch broadcast from the true first global rank of its DP group under non-contiguous parallel layouts.
observable_signal: input batch checksum equality across ranks that share the same broadcast group
validity_precondition: non-trivial parallel layout where DP groups are not contiguous global ranks (e.g. PP=2, DP=2)
evidence_from_issue: get_data_parallel_src_rank uses global_rank % num_dp_groups instead of looking up first global rank in the DP group
evidence_from_fix: formula only matches the true DP src rank when DP groups are contiguous; with PP > 1 or other interleavings, the formula returns the wrong rank

relation_statement: MoE expert gradients must be scaled by 1/dp_world_size after gradient sync, matching the averaging applied to dense gradients, under DP>1.
observable_signal: expert gradient norm exceeding the dense-equivalent averaged gradient by a factor of dp_world_size
validity_precondition: MoE expert parameters whose main_grads are local-only (num_experts >= 2)
evidence_from_issue: DistributedDataParallel.finish_grad_sync forgets to scale expert_grads by 1/dp_world_size
evidence_from_fix: syncs the regular grad buffers but never divides expert_grads; buggy expert grads are dp_world_size× larger than intended

relation_statement: Parameter-sync launches must be issued for every microbatch id up to total_num_microbatches, aligned across PP ranks, under interleaved pipelining with param_sync_func set.
observable_signal: per-step count of param-sync invocations compared against total_num_microbatches on each PP rank
validity_precondition: interleaved pipeline parallelism with config.param_sync_func set and num_model_chunks >= 3
evidence_from_issue: forward_backward_pipelining_with_interleaving uses num_microbatches instead of total_num_microbatches in the param-sync gate
evidence_from_fix: condition `param_sync_microbatch_id < num_microbatches` should be `< total_num_microbatches`; only first num_microbatches param-syncs were aligned across PP ranks

relation_statement: The second sequence-parallel all-to-all output must reconstruct the exact head-to-rank permutation of its input when num_heads is not divisible by seq_world_size.
observable_signal: element-wise mismatch of attention output against a single-rank (SP=1) reference execution
validity_precondition: sequence-parallel single_all_to_all second all2all (scatter_idx<2) with num_heads % seq_world_size != 0 and get_num_kv_heads() None
evidence_from_issue: single_all_to_all routes uneven-head path on second all2all when divisibility fails
evidence_from_fix: buggy gate routes to uneven_heads_all2all even on the second all2all; uneven path does not produce correct output for second all2all

relation_statement: Router combine weights must be post-softmax probabilities bounded in [0,1], not raw logits, whenever top-k gating selects and weights experts.
observable_signal: gate/combine weight values falling outside [0,1] (negative or greater than one, as raw logits can be)
validity_precondition: MoE top-k gating module active in forward
evidence_from_issue: TopKGate applies topk to logits instead of post-softmax gates
evidence_from_fix: torch.topk(logits, k) selects experts from raw logits, not softmax probabilities

relation_statement: The runtime sequence-parallel communication dtype must equal the user-configured seq_parallel_communication_data_type whenever that key is set.
observable_signal: dtype of sequence-parallel communication buffers compared against the configured value
validity_precondition: user sets seq_parallel_communication_data_type in the config
evidence_from_issue: seq_parallel_communication_data_type config key typo causes silent ignore
evidence_from_fix: constant uses 'seq_parallel_comm_data_type' but config uses 'seq_parallel_communication_data_type'

relation_statement: The offloaded gradient partition must accumulate rather than overwrite contributions from every backward call within a step when manual gradient accumulation is used under ZeRO-1/2 CPU offload.
observable_signal: gradient norm at optimizer step vs the sum of per-microstep gradient contributions (norm underestimated on violation)
validity_precondition: ZeRO-1/2 with CPU offload and manual gradient accumulation (multiple backward calls, micro_step_id > 0)
evidence_from_issue: ZeRO-1/2 CPU-offload gradient norm underestimated with manual GA
evidence_from_fix: copy_grads_in_partition only accumulates when ga_steps > 1, misses micro_step_id > 0 case

relation_statement: The scheduler's LR list must contain exactly one scalar entry per optimizer parameter group at every scheduler query under multi-group optimizers.
observable_signal: length and element type of get_lr() output compared against the number of optimizer param groups
validity_precondition: WarmupCosineLR with an optimizer having more than one parameter group
evidence_from_issue: WarmupCosineLR multi-group initialization returns wrong-length LR list
evidence_from_fix: get_lr_ratio returns [0.0] list instead of 0.0 scalar; get_lr returns [0.0] instead of per-group list

relation_statement: The reduce-and-partition stream must be ordered after the stream that produced the gradients (the current stream) before reading the bucket under ZeRO-3.
observable_signal: nondeterministic gradient checksums across identical reruns, or gradient mismatch vs a fully synchronous baseline execution
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 3 with asynchronous reduce_and_partition_stream and gradients produced on a non-default stream
evidence_from_issue: ZeRO-3 reduce_and_partition_stream syncs against wrong CUDA stream
evidence_from_fix: __add_grad_to_ipg_bucket uses default_stream() instead of current_stream() for reduce_and_partition_stream synchronization

relation_statement: Each scaling factor (loss scale, gradient-accumulation scale) must be applied to the loss exactly once before backward.
observable_signal: gradient magnitude off by the gradient-accumulation factor relative to a singly-scaled baseline
validity_precondition: loss scaling enabled together with gradient-accumulation loss scaling in engine backward
evidence_from_issue: Loss double-scaling in backward — scale_if_loss applied to gas_scaled_loss
evidence_from_fix: root_cause field empty in record; inferred from title

relation_statement: Gradients from multiple backward() calls within one optimizer step must all be preserved in the accumulation buffer under ZeRO-1/2 with CPU offload.
observable_signal: accumulated gradient norm at step time vs the sum of per-backward gradient contributions
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 1/2 with CPU offload and more than one backward() call per optimizer step
evidence_from_issue: ZeRO-1/2 CPU-offload gradient loss with multiple backward() per step
evidence_from_fix: root_cause field empty in record; inferred from title

relation_statement: The reduction buffer for an extra-large parameter must use the configured communication dtype (not param.dtype) so its gradient participates correctly in reduction.
observable_signal: missing or zero parameter update for the extra-large parameter despite nonzero local gradient; dtype of its reduction buffer vs comm_dtype
validity_precondition: parameter with numel exceeding the reduce bucket size and communication dtype differing from param dtype
evidence_from_issue: extra_large_param uses param.dtype instead of comm_dtype — gradient silently dropped
evidence_from_fix: root_cause field empty in record; inferred from title

relation_statement: Per-parameter optimizer state after elastic checkpoint reload must equal the state saved for that same parameter, honoring the nccl alignment padding used at save time, when world size changes.
observable_signal: per-parameter optimizer state (e.g. exp_avg) checksum before save vs after load
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 1/2 elastic checkpoint loaded with a different world size and load_optimizer_states=True
evidence_from_issue: ZeRO 1/2 elastic checkpoint optimizer state alignment ignores nccl_start_alignment_factor
evidence_from_fix: alignment used for re-flattening merged optimizer state was just world_size, but ZeRO pads by nccl_start_alignment_factor * world_size when saving; per-rank slices were misaligned and silently restored to the wrong parameters

relation_statement: Reduced gradients on the destination rank must be numerically equivalent whether the configured single-rank reduce path or the bucket allreduce path is used.
observable_signal: gradient checksum difference between runs with use_multi_rank_bucket_allreduce=False vs True
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 1/2 with use_multi_rank_bucket_allreduce=False
evidence_from_issue: ZeRO2 allreduce_bucket forces rank=None, never uses single-rank reduce path
evidence_from_fix: a hard `rank = None` reset at the top of the function silently overrides any rank passed in; the intended single-destination reduce path is never taken, producing different numerics on the receiving rank

relation_statement: After a load_module_only checkpoint load, the fp32 master weights must equal the loaded 16-bit module weights before training resumes, including when bf16 is enabled.
observable_signal: elementwise difference between the fp32 master partitions and the upcast bf16 module weights immediately after load
validity_precondition: bf16 enabled with load_checkpoint(load_module_only=True, load_optimizer_states=False)
evidence_from_issue: load_module_only with bf16 silently skips refresh_fp32_params, optimizer trains on uninitialized fp32 weights
evidence_from_fix: refresh_fp32_params() was guarded by self.fp16_enabled(), so for bf16 the high-precision master weights were never refreshed from the loaded 16-bit module

relation_statement: Trainable parameters must remain full precision and nontrainable parameters must be quantized exactly as the zero_quantized_nontrainable_weights config requests during zero.Init.
observable_signal: per-parameter dtype/quantization state of trainable vs nontrainable parameters compared against the configured policy
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 3 with zero_quantized_nontrainable_weights=True in config and no explicit constructor kwarg
evidence_from_issue: ZeRO3 quantized_nontrainable_weights flag overwrites quantized_weights instead
evidence_from_fix: the code mistakenly assigns the value to self.quantized_weights instead of self.quantized_nontrainable_weights — a copy-paste typo; trainable weights end up quantized while nontrainable weights stay full precision

relation_statement: The reduce-scatter input buffer must be cast to the configured communication_data_type exactly when it differs from the model dtype under ZeRO-3.
observable_signal: dtype of the reduce-scatter buffer at collective launch compared against the configured communication_data_type
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 3 with communication_data_type different from the model dtype
evidence_from_issue: ZeRO3 communication_data_type comparison inverted — buffer cast happens only when no cast is needed
evidence_from_fix: gate was `if self.communication_data_type == self.dtype:` — exactly backward; when the user requested a different communication dtype the buffer was NOT cast, so reduce-scatter ran on the wrong dtype

relation_statement: The gradient submitted for reduction must be the accumulated fp32 gradient buffer, not the raw bf16 param.grad, whenever grad_accum_dtype=fp32 with CPU offload.
observable_signal: reduced gradient compared against the fp32 accumulated buffer contents (precision loss and stale values witness violation)
validity_precondition: bf16 model with grad_accum_dtype=fp32, ZeRO stage 1 with CPU offload, and a parameter larger than reduce_bucket_size
evidence_from_issue: bf16+ZeRO1+CPU offload silently routes through bf16 wrapper; extra-large param uses raw param.grad instead of reduction grad
evidence_from_fix: reduction code took extra_large_param_to_reduce.grad directly instead of routing through get_gradient_for_reduction(); the accumulated fp32 grad was bypassed and the raw bf16 grad was reduced

relation_statement: After optimizer.step(), each rank's 16-bit parameter partition must equal the cast of its own fp32 master partition, using each param group's own process-group rank, under MoE with expert-parallel groups.
observable_signal: elementwise difference between each rank's bit16 partition and its corresponding fp32 master partition after step
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 2 with MoE where expert parallel groups differ from the data parallel group
evidence_from_issue: ZeRO2 + MoE: fp32→fp16 master-weight copy uses outer-loop partition_id, writing into wrong rank's slice
evidence_from_fix: the loop used a single partition_id from the outer scope; with MoE different param groups use different real_dp_process_group, so the wrong partition slot was overwritten and the local rank's actual partition was never updated

relation_statement: The fp32-to-16-bit writeback after the offloaded optimizer step must target each param group's own rank partition, so every 16-bit partition equals its fp32 master partition.
observable_signal: per-group elementwise difference between bit16 partitions and their fp32 master partitions after step
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 2 with DeepSpeedCPUAdam offload and multiple param groups using different real_dp_process_group
evidence_from_issue: ZeRO2 + CPU offload: DeepSpeedCPUAdam fp32→fp16 partition_id is wrong across param groups
evidence_from_fix: the code used a single outer-scope partition_id for all groups instead of computing the rank within each group's real_dp_process_group; every group except the first received the wrong rank's partition

relation_statement: The param-to-partition-owner bookkeeping table must agree with the actual round-robin gradient reduction destination for every parameter under ZeRO-2 with round_robin_gradients.
observable_signal: parameters whose weights never change across steps despite nonzero gradients (gradient attributed to the wrong owner)
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 2 with round_robin_gradients=True
evidence_from_issue: ZeRO2 round-robin gradient partitioning uses non-reordered group, mapping params to wrong partition owner
evidence_from_fix: bookkeeping iterated over self.fp16_groups (original order) while reduction uses self.round_robin_fp16_groups; some params' gradients were attributed to the wrong owner and never appeared in the optimizer step

relation_statement: The pipeline partition boundary list must be a monotone cover assigning at least one layer to every stage when constructing pipeline modules.
observable_signal: per-stage layer or parameter count (a stage owning zero layers/parameters witnesses the violation)
validity_precondition: pipeline parallel with num_stages > 2 and uniform layer weights
evidence_from_issue: Pipeline partition_balanced returns degenerate partitions, last PP stage can be assigned zero layers
evidence_from_fix: binary-search probe returned a non-monotone boundary list like [0,2,4,5,5] for 5 items / 4 parts — the last stage owns 0 layers; pipeline modules silently train with a stage holding no parameters

relation_statement: Exactly one rank must write each consolidated non-ZeRO checkpoint file per save operation under MiCS partitioning.
observable_signal: count of ranks writing the same checkpoint file path per save (more than one witnesses the race)
validity_precondition: MiCS sharding with world_size > mics_shard_size and save_checkpoint called on all ranks
evidence_from_issue: MiCS save_non_zero_checkpoint True on every rank — checkpoint files race-overwrite each other
evidence_from_fix: save_non_zero_checkpoint became True for every MiCS rank because zero_optimization_partition_weights() is True under MiCS; all ranks wrote the consolidated file, racing and leaving inconsistent contents

relation_statement: The allgather partition buffer must match each parameter's own dtype when a parameter group mixes floating dtypes under ZeRO-3.
observable_signal: parameter checksum/NaN scan after allgather compared against the rank-local shard contents (garbage bit patterns witness violation)
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 3 with a model containing parameters of more than one floating dtype
evidence_from_issue: ZeRO3 allgather hardcodes ds_tensor dtype — mixed-dtype param groups silently allgather wrong bytes
evidence_from_fix: one flat partition buffer assumed a single ds_tensor dtype; larger-dtype params were silently truncated/aliased into the smaller-dtype buffer, so parameters held garbage bit patterns after allgather

relation_statement: A parameter may be consumed in forward only after its own coordinator's allgather completes; train and eval coordinators must not observe each other's in-flight handles.
observable_signal: stale parameter checksums (values unchanged from the previous mode's shards) in the first iteration after a train/eval switch
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 3 with prefetch/overlap_comm and alternating model.train()/model.eval() inside a step
evidence_from_issue: ZeRO3 InflightParamRegistry shared between train and eval coordinators causes stale handles on mode switch
evidence_from_fix: both coordinators were constructed with the same shared InflightParamRegistry; on mode switch one coordinator observed the other's in-flight handles, leading to silently-stale parameter values

relation_statement: Allreduced sparse gradients must be written back into the parameter's grad so no gradient contribution is dropped under DP>1.
observable_signal: sparse embedding parameters showing zero update across steps despite nonzero local gradients
validity_precondition: modules producing sparse gradients (e.g. embedding with sparse=True)
evidence_from_issue: Sparse gradients silently not updating — SparseTensor wraps .data instead of param.grad
evidence_from_fix: Python re-bound the local name and never wrote back into param.grad; the post-allreduce values lived on a temporary SparseTensor with no link to the parameter — sparse embedding gradients were silently dropped

relation_statement: The loss broadcast receive buffer on non-last PP stages must have the same dtype as the sent loss tensor so every stage observes the same loss value.
observable_signal: loss value on non-last PP stages compared against the last stage's aggregated loss (equality check per step)
validity_precondition: pipeline parallel with a bf16 model loss tensor and loss aggregation broadcast to all stages
evidence_from_issue: Pipeline parallel _aggregate_total_loss broadcasts torch.stack of mixed-dtype losses, non-last stages receive wrong dtype
evidence_from_fix: the broadcast tensor was bf16 but other ranks initialised their receive buffer as fp32; dist.broadcast wrote bf16 bytes into an fp32 tensor and other PP stages saw garbage scalar losses
